original_question: Classify finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^(n+2). Here finite type means that the position vector of the immersed hypersurface is a finite sum of Laplace eigenmaps.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Problem 3: "Classify finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^{n+2}."
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper’s exact target almost verbatim: the problem in the paper is precisely to classify finite type hypersurfaces lying in a hypersphere of E^{n+2}. Your added gloss on “finite type” also matches the paper’s core definition that the Euclidean position vector decomposes into finitely many Laplace eigenmaps.
missing_details: The paper’s notion is for an isometric immersion x: M^n -> E^{n+2} of a connected Riemannian manifold, with M^n a hypersurface of some hypersphere S^{n+1} ⊂ E^{n+2}; this ambient setup should be stated explicitly.
Finite type is taken with respect to the Euclidean position vector x: M -> E^{n+2}, not merely as a hypersurface of S^{n+1} in an intrinsic spherical sense.
The spectral decomposition in the paper includes a constant vector term: x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k.
The summands x_i are required to be nonconstant E^{n+2}-valued maps satisfying Δx_i = λ_i x_i.
Δ is the Laplace operator on M induced from the immersed Riemannian metric; this should be named explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
Problem 3 has no compactness assumption, so a refined version should not accidentally insert one.
The paper separates the 2-type case as Problem 2; Problem 3 asks for all finite-type hypersurfaces, i.e. arbitrary finite type number k, not just k = 2.
To stay paper-faithful, the refined question should say “hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^{n+2}” rather than something broader such as arbitrary spherical submanifolds.
refined_question: Let x: M^n -> S^{n+1} \subset E^{n+2} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold as a hypersurface of a hypersphere in Euclidean space. Classify those hypersurfaces for which, viewed as an immersion into E^{n+2}, the position vector field is of finite Chen type; that is, x admits a finite spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k with c \in E^{n+2} constant, each x_i a nonconstant E^{n+2}-valued map on M, and Δx_i = λ_i x_i for the Laplace operator Δ of M.
justification: The closest official formulation is exactly Section 4.1, Problem 3. The draft is already very close, but to make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper one must import the Section 2.1 definition of finite type: the problem concerns isometric immersions of connected Riemannian manifolds into Euclidean space, with finite type defined via a Euclidean spectral decomposition of the position vector including a constant term. The nearby Section 4.1 context also shows that this is not merely the 2-type classification problem: Problem 2 handles 2-type hypersurfaces separately, while Problem 3 asks for all finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere. The follow-up discussion and Conjecture 2 further confirm that the unresolved difficulty is the higher-type spherical case, especially beyond type 2.
